Opposition outlets and independent technology monitors allege signs of digital synthesis in the Governor's recent broadcasts. Officials dismiss the claims as foreign-sponsored disinformation. Press-freedom groups have expressed concern that the label is being used to discourage reporting on the Governor's absence. In a March survey by the Talas State University Institute of Sociology, 58 percent of ISEZ respondents said official information about the Governor's health was insufficient.

Ruslan Toktarov, who commands the Gendarmerie, and Alikhan Toktarov, who chairs IradOne, have both appeared in public far more often since mid-2024, and the friction between them over the succession is publicly evident. Analysts say February's anti-American protests made Alikhan's Western-leaning image a liability. Tabloids in Talas have reported family tensions over access to the Boz-Korgon estate; these reports are unverified, and the family has not commented. The DPI has named no successor, and the next election is due in November 2027.

headline: Kurultai Sets Terms for 2027 Naryn Talks
dek: The clan assembly has instructed its delegation for the renewal of the Naryn schedule and repeated that the clans “know no guests among their own”.
paragraphs: The Kurultai of the Iradi Freedom Society, meeting on the Aksay Plateau, has instructed the IAC delegation for the 2027 renewal of the Naryn Water and Power Protocol’s five-year schedule, the Chancellery said in a letter to the UN mission at Kara-Oi.

According to the Chancellery, the delegation is to agree to no new schedule unless the ISEZ is represented by an official able to sign in person, and unless the fund for Toktogul-basin families agreed after the long Kurultai of 2022 continues under it. Delegates said the instructions echoed Bektur Zhumabek uulu’s statement last November that the IAC would “not negotiate with a recording”.

The Department of Public Information said Governor Erlan Toktarov continues to govern from his health retreat and that Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat signs on his behalf. It rejected suggestions that the Governor’s recorded addresses are not genuine.

The assembly also condemned remarks made in December by the commander of the Gendarmerie describing Muslims of the Fergana Rim as “guests”. Its statement said the clans “know no guests among their own”. Chubar elders, who joined Sunni clerics in condemning the remarks at the time, supported the wording. The Department of Public Information has said the remarks reflected personal views.

headline: The episode America forgot
dek: Withdrawn from American television after one broadcast in 1994, “The Steppe Family Robinson” returns to IradOne this week, three decades after its first Iradi broadcast, and this year Iradis are watching it differently.
paragraphs: In the United States it aired once, on 3 February 1994, and then disappeared: withdrawn from reruns, syndication and home video under a 1995 settlement over its parody of the Swift Hooves single “Ride for Talas”, and left off every streaming release since. American fans call it a lost episode. In Irad it has never been lost. IradOne will show “The Steppe Family Robinson” this week, dubbed into Iradi, in the week of the Feast of St. Janyl, as it has almost every year since August 1995.

This year the familiar scenes land differently. After US President Donald Trump’s remarks in February about selling Irad to Russia, clips of the High Commissioner summoning Homer, and telling him that the United States had spent eighteen months persuading Iradis that Americans are not Russians, circulated widely on Iradi social media, shared with captions that needed no translation.
“In 1994 the joke was that Americans didn’t know where Irad was,” said one Talas State University student who has watched the episode every summer since childhood. “Now it looks like a documentary.”
Under the settlement, the license fees for the Iradi broadcasts go to charity, since 2001 to the St. Luka Community Health Mission.

headline: Tulpar says it has won back the users it lost in the spring
dek: Monthly users are above their January level, the company says, helped by voice notes, a cheaper data mode and the end of the boycott posts.
paragraphs: The messaging app Tulpar said yesterday that its monthly users had passed 590,000, above their level before the spring's "American app" campaign, when about a sixth of users left after the US President's remarks about Irad.

The company credited a low-data mode launched in May, voice notes in Iradi and Russian, and the return of Bazar sellers during the summer livestock season. Kubat Toktogul uulu, a sheep trader at the Kara-Buura market who sells through the app, said he had left in March "because my cousin said it was a spy" and came back in June "because my customers never left".
Analysts said the boycott posts had faded as attention moved to the Governor's continued absence. Tulpar's figures are not independently audited.

Jason Ilyasov, the app's founder, said the episode had taught him "that Iradis forgive a passport faster than a slow app". He said the company was preparing "new services" for next year, without giving details.

headline: A Year Out, Nurzhan Lists Weigh a Joint Ticket
dek: Russo-aligned deputies and union officials are discussing a single opposition ticket for November 2027, with Oleg Zubarev and Elena Petrova both mentioned.
paragraphs: With the general election fixed for 2 November 2027, the Russo-aligned civic lists of Nurzhan have begun talks on fielding a single ticket for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, according to deputies and union officials who spoke to the Herald.

The name most often mentioned is Oleg Zubarev, the engineer and city councillor who was runner-up in 2023 with an official 4.61 percent, and a little over 11 percent in Nurzhan. Trade-union circles have floated an alternative ticket led by the councillor Elena Petrova, recalling the union-backed nominee struck from the ballot in 2015. Neither has declared. Any ticket will need 10,000 verified signatures and candidates with ten years’ continuous residence under the Election Commission’s 2015 rules.

The three Russo-aligned deputies in the legislature, elected on lists funded largely by businessmen linked to NurGaz, form its only consistent opposition. Kamran Bekzatov has never stood for office or endorsed a candidate, and NurGaz declined to comment.

The Democratic Party of Irad has not said whether Governor Erlan Toktarov will stand again or who will lead its ticket, saying only that it will announce it “at the proper time”. The commentator Jason Ilyasov, who will meet the residence rule in 2027, has said he has “not ruled anything out”.

headline: Supreme Court Petition on Governor's Health Awaits Listing
dek: Three months after it was filed, the petition asking the court to interpret the Elective Governor Acts on a Governor’s inability has not been scheduled for a hearing.
paragraphs: A petition asking the Supreme Court to rule on how the Elective Governor Acts apply when a Governor is unable to act has not been listed for hearing, three months after it was filed, the court registry confirmed yesterday.

The petition, In re the Elective Governor Acts (Inability of the Governor), was filed in June by the Talas lawyer Nazira Abdykadyr and the Nurzhan lawyer Vitaly Kuzmenko on behalf of the three Russo-aligned deputies, after the legislature declined their request for a hearing on the Governor’s health. It asks whether a formal declaration of inability is required before the Lieutenant Governor exercises the Governor’s powers, who is competent to make it, and whether a Governor unable to appear may be nominated for the 2027 election.

Government counsel have asked the court to decline the questions as hypothetical, arguing that they belong to the legislature, as the court held on term limits in 2014. The government’s position is that the Governor, on an extended health retreat since July 2024, continues in office and that Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat acts on his instructions.

In a March survey by the Talas State University Institute of Sociology, 61 percent of respondents said official information about the Governor’s health was insufficient, up from 58 percent a year earlier. The Department of Public Information said this month that the OSCE would be invited to observe the 2027 election “as in previous elections”.

headline: Tulpar Pay to drop the som for Tulparcoin in January, white paper says
dek: Transfers, Bazar purchases and remittances inside the messaging app would be settled only in the new coin from 1 January, with shops swapping cash for coins.
paragraphs: Tulpar Pay, the payment service that the messaging app Tulpar plans to open inside its chats, will settle payments only in Tulparcoin from 1 January 2027, according to the coin's white paper, a reading of which was confirmed by the Liberty Forum yesterday.

Under the plan, users would buy coins with cash som or dollars at shops acting as "Tulpar points", send them to one another in chat, pay for Bazar listings and receive transfers from relatives abroad. Coins held in the app would earn a yearly reward of 6 percent, paid in new coins. The paper says nothing about how users could turn coins back into cash if the points run short.

Jason Ilyasov, the app's founder, said the aim was to give Iradis "money the family can't freeze, ration or count" and a way out of "the shrinking som and the rationed dollar", a reference to the limits on dollar withdrawals that Talasbank introduced in May.

Bolot Ormokoev of Talas State University said the plan would put household savings into an asset that had moved between four and seven US cents in its first two days. "It is one thing to give people a free coin," he said. "It is another to make them hold their wages in it."

headline: Bank of Irad: Tulpar Pay would need a licence it does not have
dek: The currency board says a payment service inside the messaging app falls under the 1993 Act, whatever coin it uses. Tulpar says the bank has already ruled the coin is not money.
paragraphs: The Bank of Irad said yesterday that Tulpar Pay, the payment service the messaging app Tulpar plans to run in Tulparcoin from January, would be an unlicensed payment and deposit-taking service under the Banking and Commercial Currency Act of 1993, and that any business taking part could face penalties.

Ermek Sadykbekov, a deputy chairman, said the bank's warning last week that Tulparcoin was not legal tender "does not mean that anyone may take the public's som and dollars in exchange for it without a licence". He said the bank would write to shops advertising themselves as "Tulpar points".

Tulpar Technologies replied in a statement that "by the bank's own words, Tulparcoin is not money, so a service that moves it is not a bank". The company said it had no presence in the ISEZ that the bank could license.

The Lieutenant Governor's office said it supported the bank. Kamran Bekzatov, the president of NurGaz, said in an interview with IradOdin that the coin was "a toy that can burn down a house" and that "a country with a fixed currency and no central bank of its own cannot afford experiments run from Chicago".

headline: Bazaar rate passes 11 som as dollar cash runs short; Bank of Irad says peg is safe
dek: Money changers in Talas and Nurzhan are asking more than 11 som for a dollar against the official 8.40. The bank says its reserves cover every som in circulation.
paragraphs: Money changers at the central bazaar in Talas and the central market in Nurzhan were asking between 11 and 11.6 som for a US dollar yesterday, against the Bank of Irad's official rate of 8.40, as the shortage of dollar banknotes that began in the spring continued.

Talasbank has limited cash dollar withdrawals and som-to-dollar conversions to US$300 a month per customer since May, citing reduced shipments of banknotes from its correspondent banks in Almaty. Traders said the limit had pushed importers and families saving for weddings and migration to the unlicensed changers. In June the street rate was about 9.5.

The Bank of Irad said its reserves fully covered the som in circulation, that the official rate was unchanged and that no adjustment was planned. A spokesman called the bazaar quotations "speculation in a small cash market". Older traders were not reassured. "In 2008 they also said the rate was safe, until the morning it was 8.40," said a changer in Nurzhan who has worked at the market since 1996.

Most shops, utilities and public transport still price and accept som at the official rate. Sellers of imported goods increasingly ask for dollars, and the online marketplace Jılmay said this week that goods bought abroad through its cargo service would be sold in dollars only.
